_note_on_types: Every numeric value in this file is a STRING, deliberately.
json.load turns a JSON number into a Python float, and FMT-02 forbids float money.
A commutation factor of 12.3719 read as a float and multiplied by a gross pension is
exactly the class of silent precision loss the rule exists to prevent, so the loader
refuses floats and converts these strings with Decimal instead.

QS-01.description: Qualifying service runs from first regular entry to retirement, death, or notional superannuation.
QS-01.citation: Punjab Civil Services Pension Rules; BRAIN §9.1

QS-07.description: Fractions of a year: 6 months or more rounds up to a full year; less than 6 months is ignored.
QS-07.citation: Punjab Civil Services Pension Rules; BRAIN §9.1

QS-08.description: A maximum of 30 years is reckoned for pension. At the cap the gross pension is 70% of emoluments.
QS-08.citation: Punjab Civil Services Pension Rules; BRAIN §9.1

QS-10.description: Superannuation at age 60, taking effect on the afternoon of the day preceding the 60th birthday.
QS-10.citation: Punjab Civil Services Pension Rules; BRAIN §9.1

QS-16.description: Day-counting convention for qualifying service is EXCLUSIVE of the date of first entry.
QS-16.citation: BRAIN §9.1; convention fixed by this pack

EMOL-BASE.description: Reckonable emoluments are the LAST DRAWN reckonable pay, not a 24-month average.
EMOL-BASE.citation: Punjab FD; federal 24-month averaging NOT adopted for Punjab on present evidence

CALC-01.description: Gross pension per month = reckonable emoluments x qualifying service x 7 / 300.
CALC-01.citation: Punjab Civil Services Pension Rules; BRAIN §9.2

FAM-IS-01.description: On death in service the deceased's pay continues to the family until the notional superannuation date; family pension commences thereafter.

FAM-IS-03.description: Family pension = gross pension x 75/100 per month.
FAM-IS-03.citation: Punjab FD reformed pension procedure; BRAIN §9.7

FAM-IS-04.description: Gratuity on death in service. INTERPRETATION DISPUTED - two readings, no single figure.

FAM-IS-05.description: Family pension commences the day after the notional superannuation date.

ADD-02.description: Medical allowance: 25% of pension for BPS 1-15, 20% for BPS 16 and above. BASE DISPUTED.

ADD-03.description: Minimum pension and minimum family pension floors, per FD notification.
ADD-03.citation: Punjab FD notification - current values not loaded

COMM-01.description: Punjab maximum commutation is 35% of gross pension. The federal 25% does NOT apply to Punjab.

COMM-TABLE.description: Age factor by age next birthday. The loaded table is INCOMPLETE - four benchmark ages only.
COMM-TABLE.citation: Pension Rules / Compendium 2018 - full table not yet obtained

FMT-01.description: Monthly pension amounts round to the nearest whole rupee, half up.

EMOL-07.description: Orderly allowance. Whether it is reckonable for pension is DISPUTED - three project sources give three readings. No determination may sum it either way until resolved.
EMOL-07.citation: BRAIN §9.3 lists EMOL-07 as reckonable; Form B-I/D-I Note 2 lists only the six components and places 'Orderly Allowance (if any)' as a separate numbered clause OUTSIDE 'Total pay'; scope/ai-system-scope §3.2 says '6-component reckonable pay + orderly allowance'

_note_on_reckonable_components: The closed list of Note 2, as component names. extraction/classify.py maps a PRINTED
LABEL onto one of these names - that is a reading task. Whether a name is reckonable
is a RULE with a rupee consequence, so it lives here, in versioned data, and is the
single source of truth the engine sums against.
On the golden case the excluded allowances total 161,765 against reckonable pay of
192,030: moving one label across this line changes a pension for life.
_note_on_disputed_components: orderly_allowance is NOT in reckonable_components and NOT simply excluded either.
The prescribed form prints the six Note-2 components, closes them with 'Total pay Rs.',
and then asks for '(2) Orderly Allowance (if any) Rs. ____' as a separate clause. That
layout is also what made the vision model report 'Orderly Allowance 192,030' -- it paired
the printed total with the label that follows it.
Summing it would overstate a pension for life; excluding it would understate one. So a
case that actually carries an orderly allowance raises and routes to human determination
(BRAIN §15.1: never resolve a BLOCKING item by reasoning).

_note_on_dating: This pack states the rules as they stood BEFORE the Finance Department amendment of
2 December 2024 (NO.FD.SR-III-4-244/2023(B)). It was originally dated from 2026-01-01,
which cannot be right: by then the amendment had been in force for more than a year,
and this pack contradicts it on the pension base, the commutation ceiling and the
duration of a spouse's family pension.
The END date is exact -- the amendment took effect the following day. The START date is
approximate: it is the date of FD.SR-1/3-10/2004 of 15-08-2017, the notification behind
the family-pension rules here, and is the earliest date this pack can be said to state.
A case whose governing date falls before it will be refused rather than computed on a
pack that does not claim to cover it.
It is kept, not deleted: a pension sanctioned under the old rules was lawfully sanctioned
under them, and an audit years from now must be able to recompute what was actually paid.

_blocking_21_pack_selection.question: Which date selects the rule pack for a death in service: the date of death, or the notional superannuation date on which the family pension commences?
_blocking_21_pack_selection.why_it_matters: The December 2024 amendment falls between the two on the reference case. Death 29-07-2021 selects the pre-amendment pack; notional superannuation 18-02-2026 selects the amended one, which narrows the base from six pay components to a three-year average of two. The same case computes differently depending on the answer.
_blocking_21_pack_selection.assumed_pending_a_ruling: The date of the event. A pension right crystallises when the servant dies or retires, and this engine will not apply an amendment made three years after a death unless told to.
